---
title: "Help improve the handbook"
---

If an explanation is confusing or a question is missing, tell us. A few specific sentences can help the next researcher who gets stuck in the same place.

[Suggest an improvement](https://github.com/hareshsuppiah/handbook-for-the-recently-enrolled/issues/new?template=share-feedback.yml){.btn .btn-primary}

You'll need a free GitHub account. GitHub calls a suggestion an **issue**: a page where you and an editor can discuss the change. You don't need to know Git or rewrite the chapter yourself. The [step-by-step guide](how-to-help.qmd) walks you through it.

## What to send

You can suggest a missing topic, correct advice, share a source, propose a shorter explanation or point out something that's hard to read. If advice only applies in your discipline or university, say so. The form works for all of these.

Include the page link, what you noticed and what would help. Send separate suggestions for unrelated changes so each gets a clear response.

GitHub submissions are public. Keep personal details, participant data, private correspondence and confidential research out of the form. For a personal or urgent concern, use the services listed in [Local rules and specialist help](../support.qmd).

## After you submit

An editor reads the suggestion, checks existing coverage and may ask you for a detail or source. You'll receive a decision on the same page. Accepted ideas move to drafting, which a contributor or AI agent may help with. An authorised editor reviews the proposed edits before publication.

You can choose how you'd like to be credited, including no public credit. The [suggestion tracker](tracker.qmd) shows the discussion and any published change.

For more detail, read about [editorial decisions](editorial-workflow.qmd), [AI assistance](ai-and-editorial-practice.qmd) and [images and credit](visuals-and-credit.qmd).
